entities.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the Creator who names the light Day and the darkness Night. The existing source tag identifies this bearer as LORD@Gen.1.1.

name_review_base.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the Creator who names the light Day and the darkness Night. The existing source tag identifies this bearer as LORD@Gen.1.1.

review.translation: [And|0] [God|1] [called|0] [the light|2] [Day|3], [and the darkness|4] [he called|5] [Night|6]. [Then there was|7] [evening|8], [and there was|9] [morning|10], [one|12] [day|11].

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, לָאוֹר identifies the light as what God names, and יוֹם supplies its name, “Day.” The parallel clause gives the darkness its corresponding name, לָיְלָה, “Night.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּקְרָא, a third-person masculine singular verb. God names the light Day, and the parallel clause uses the singular קָרָא for his naming of the darkness Night.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם, לָאוֹר designates what God names and יוֹם gives its name, “Day.” The parallel clause pairs darkness with the name “Night,” establishing the contrast between light and darkness.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ with the definite article (לָ־) prefixed to a common-gender singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: God calls the light (לָאוֹר) יוֹם, just as he calls the darkness (וְלַחֹשֶׁךְ) לָיְלָה. The parallel naming identifies יוֹם as the light portion of the day.
analysis.sense: daylight, the day as against night

analysis.evidence: God calls the light יוֹם ‘day’ and the darkness לָיְלָה ‘night’. The parallel names identify חֹשֶׁךְ as the absence of light.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed conjunction וְ and preposition לְ combined with the definite article as לַ.

analysis.evidence: The two clauses share the subject אֱלֹהִים. Just as God names the light יוֹם, the phrase וְלַחֹשֶׁךְ קָרָא לָיְלָה places the darkness before the verb and gives לָיְלָה (‘Night’) as its name.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: God calls the light יוֹם and the darkness לָיְלָה. The parallel naming clauses identify לָיְלָה as the name for the dark part of the day.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun in pausal form.

analysis.evidence: עֶרֶב is the subject of וַיְהִי. The parallel clauses וַיְהִי עֶרֶב and וַיְהִי בֹקֶר recount the arrival of evening and then morning.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed consecutive וַ.

analysis.evidence: The parallel clauses וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר mean “there was evening and there was morning.” The pairing with בֹקֶר identifies עֶרֶב as the time of day.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular, absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי בֹקֶר, בֹקֶר is the subject. The preceding וַיְהִי עֶרֶב marks the arrival of evening, and the repeated verb marks the arrival of morning.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־. The verb agrees with its subject בֹקֶר.

analysis.evidence: The parallel clauses וַיְהִי עֶרֶב and וַיְהִי בֹקֶר pair evening with morning as the verse recounts the first day.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After evening and morning, אֶחָד counts the elapsed day in יוֹם אֶחָד, “one day.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר, “there was evening and there was morning,” יוֹם אֶחָד labels the completed day “day one.” The cardinal אֶחָד marks its first place in the count.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, masculine singular absolute, agreeing with יוֹם.
analysis.sense: first (in a count, and of dates)
